topic.title: Grounding and Hallucination in Multimodal Reasoning
topic.overview: A multimodal model can produce a fluent answer that is unsupported by its visual input, even when it recognizes individual objects correctly. These papers study object, relationship, and compositional hallucinations, alongside verification and inference-time correction. They examine how language priors, attention routes, and accumulated reasoning can override relevant evidence.
topic.whyItMatters: Attention to an image does not prove that the final decision used it correctly. Reliable grounding requires checking relationships and reasoning dependencies, not merely whether visual tokens appeared somewhere in the computation.
topic.evolution: The 2024 representatives establish targeted hallucination evaluations and contrastive decoding ideas. Later work adds compositional benchmarks, visual retracing, and retrospective verification. Recent analyses distinguish visual and textual routes and study confidence fluctuations or reused reasoning paths, seeking mechanisms that explain why unsupported conclusions persist.
openQuestions: Which interventions reduce hallucination without suppressing correct use of prior knowledge?
How can a benchmark separate visual recognition errors from failures of composition and reasoning?

papers.tldr: R-Bench evaluates invented visual relationships and reveals how learned associations can outweigh image evidence in vision-language models.

papers.tldr: HALC reduces object hallucinations without extra training by combining local visual grounding with global decoding search.

papers.tldr: Language models can compound an initial wrong answer with false claims they can recognize as incorrect when evaluated separately.

papers.tldr: An entropy-based signal from contextual hidden states helps adjust language-model decoding and reduce factual errors.

papers.title: Alleviating Hallucinations in Large Vision-Language Models through Hallucination-Induced Optimization
papers.tldr: HIO reduces visual hallucinations by learning to sharpen the token-score contrast used in contrastive decoding.

papers.title: CODE: Contrasting Self-generated Description to Combat Hallucination in Large Multi-modal Models
papers.tldr: CODE uses a multimodal model’s own image descriptions as contrastive decoding references to reduce visual hallucinations without additional training.

papers.title: Estimating the Hallucination Rate of Generative AI
papers.tldr: A Bayesian framework estimates in-context hallucination rates using generated questions, responses, and response log probabilities.

papers.title: HaloScope: Harnessing Unlabeled LLM Generations for Hallucination Detection
papers.tldr: HaloScope learns a hallucination detector from automatically scored, unlabeled language-model outputs without additional human annotation.

papers.title: I Don't Know: Explicit Modeling of Uncertainty with an [IDK] Token
papers.tldr: Training language models to assign incorrect predictions’ probability to an [IDK] token helps them express uncertainty with a small reported knowledge loss.

papers.title: Leveraging Hallucinations to Reduce Manual Prompt Dependency in Promptable Segmentation
papers.tldr: ProMaC iteratively checks and refines hallucination-derived context through prompt and mask generation to reduce reliance on object-specific manual prompts.

papers.title: LLM-Check: Investigating Detection of Hallucinations in Large Language Models
papers.tldr: LLM-Check detects hallucinations in single responses using auxiliary-model signals, with improved detection and substantial reported speedups.

papers.title: Mitigating Object Hallucination via Concentric Causal Attention
papers.tldr: Concentric Causal Attention reduces visual-instruction token distances to mitigate RoPE-related object hallucination in vision-language models.

papers.title: Multi-Object Hallucination in Vision Language Models
papers.tldr: ROPE reveals that tested vision-language models hallucinate more when attending to multiple objects, with behavior affected by object distributions and other factors.

papers.title: Toward a Stable, Fair, and Comprehensive Evaluation of Object Hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models
papers.tldr: LeHaCE compares object hallucination at matched description lengths and measures how hallucination grows with verbosity.

papers.title: Unleashing Region Understanding in Intermediate Layers for MLLM-based Referring Expression Generation
papers.tldr: A training-free decoding framework uses intermediate-layer region information to improve referring descriptions and reduce hallucinations.

papers.title: Look Twice Before You Answer: Memory-Space Visual Retracing for Hallucination Mitigation in Multimodal Large Language Models
papers.tldr: MemVR reinjects visual evidence when a multimodal model becomes uncertain during decoding, reducing hallucinations without reported additional time overhead.

papers.title: Mitigating Object Hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models via Image-Grounded Guidance
papers.tldr: MARINE uses open-source vision models to guide image descriptions at inference, reducing object hallucination without training or API access.

papers.title: MMedPO: Aligning Medical Vision-Language Models with Clinical-Aware Multimodal Preference Optimization
papers.tldr: MMedPO uses clinically relevant response errors and lesion-region corruption to improve medical vision-language models’ factual accuracy.

papers.title: Robust Multimodal Large Language Models Against Modality Conflict
papers.tldr: A new dataset and three mitigation approaches expose modality conflict as a hallucination source, with reinforcement learning performing best in the reported evaluation.

papers.title: SECOND: Mitigating Perceptual Hallucination in Vision-Language Models via Selective and Contrastive Decoding
papers.tldr: SECOND reduces visual hallucinations by progressively selecting and contrasting object-centered information across image scales.

papers.title: Steer LLM Latents for Hallucination Detection
papers.tldr: TSV steers language-model representations to improve hallucination detection using a small labeled set and filtered pseudo-labels.

papers.title: The Hidden Life of Tokens: Reducing Hallucination of Large Vision-Language Models Via Visual Information Steering
papers.tldr: VISTA steers existing visual and early-layer signals during inference, reducing hallucination by about 40% on the evaluated open-ended generation task.

papers.title: AHa-Bench: Benchmarking Audio Hallucinations in Large Audio-Language Models
papers.tldr: AHa-Bench separates audio hallucinations into three categories and reveals difficulties combining sound properties with meaning.

papers.title: Alleviating Hallucinations in Large Language Models through Multi-Model Contrastive Decoding and Dynamic Hallucination Detection
papers.tldr: Multi-Model Contrastive Decoding combines three models with token-level detection and tree-based revision to reduce reported hallucinations.

papers.title: AVCD: Mitigating Hallucinations in Audio-Visual Large Language Models through Contrastive Decoding
papers.tldr: AVCD uses modality-aware, training-free contrastive decoding to reduce hallucinations in audio-visual language models.

papers.title: Between Reality and AI Hallucinations: Reimagining the Sacred Soundscape of Ming Rituals
papers.tldr: An interactive installation combines reconstructed Ming ritual soundscapes with AI hallucinations to explore cultural memory and spiritual experience.

papers.title: Beyond Token Probes: Hallucination Detection via Activation Tensors with ACT-ViT
papers.tldr: ACT-ViT detects hallucinations by analyzing activation patterns across layers and tokens, benefiting from training on multiple language models.

papers.title: Controlled Visual Hallucination via Thalamus-Driven Decoupling Network for Domain Adaptation of Black-Box Predictors
papers.tldr: CVH-TDN uses controlled feature-space sample generation to improve black-box domain adaptation, reporting state-of-the-art results on four benchmarks.

papers.title: Decoupling Contrastive Decoding: Robust Hallucination Mitigation in Multimodal Large Language Models
papers.tldr: DCD separately learns positive and negative image projections to suppress hallucinations while preserving general reasoning performance in the reported evaluations.

papers.title: Discovering Compositional Hallucinations in LVLMs
papers.tldr: The paper identifies hallucinations caused by combining otherwise successful visual and language processing, and introduces a benchmark and mitigation method.

papers.title: Do LVLMs Truly Understand Video Anomalies? Revealing Hallucination via Co-Occurrence Patterns
papers.tldr: The paper identifies co-occurrence shortcuts in video anomaly judgments and improves contextual reasoning using preference training on contrasting video pairs.

papers.title: Enhancing Vision-Language Model Reliability with Uncertainty-Guided Dropout Decoding
papers.tldr: Dropout Decoding masks uncertain visual tokens and aggregates predictions to reduce hallucinations.

papers.title: Generate, but Verify: Reducing Hallucination in Vision-Language Models with Retrospective Resampling
papers.tldr: REVERSE trains vision-language models to detect hallucinations and revise them during generation through retrospective resampling.

papers.title: GLSim: Detecting Object Hallucinations in LVLMs via Global-Local Similarity
papers.tldr: GLSim combines global and local image-text similarity to detect object hallucinations without additional training.

papers.title: Grounding Language with Vision: A Conditional Mutual Information Calibrated Decoding Strategy for Reducing Hallucinations in LVLMs
papers.tldr: A mutual-information-based decoding method jointly refines visual and text tokens to reduce image-irrelevant responses while preserving decoding efficiency.

papers.title: Image Token Matters: Mitigating Hallucination in Discrete Tokenizer-based Large Vision-Language Models via Latent Editing
papers.tldr: Editing latent image embeddings to suppress associated but absent image tokens reduces hallucinations while preserving expressivity in the reported experiments.

papers.title: Intervene-All-Paths: Unified Mitigation of LVLM Hallucinations across Alignment Formats
papers.tldr: Targeting hallucination-related attention heads across multiple information pathways reduces vision-language hallucinations across different question-answer formats.

papers.title: MIRAGE: Assessing Hallucination in Multimodal Reasoning Chains of MLLM
papers.tldr: MIRAGE isolates reasoning hallucinations after correct image perception, while Logos reduces them through curriculum training and collaborative hints.

papers.title: Mitigating Hallucination in VideoLLMs via Temporal-Aware Activation Engineering
papers.tldr: A temporally aware activation framework reduces video-model hallucinations by adaptively modifying sensitive internal modules without additional fine-tuning.

papers.title: Mitigating Hallucination Through Theory-Consistent Symmetric Multimodal Preference Optimization
papers.tldr: SymMPO combines theoretically aligned symmetric preference learning with preference-gap consistency to reduce multimodal hallucination across five benchmarks.

papers.title: On Epistemic Uncertainty of Visual Tokens for Object Hallucinations in Large Vision-Language Models
papers.tldr: Identifying unstable visual tokens and masking their influence inside the vision encoder reduces object hallucinations in the reported experiments.

papers.title: One SPACE to Rule Them All: Jointly Mitigating Factuality and Faithfulness Hallucinations in LLMs
papers.tldr: SPACE edits shared activation subspaces to jointly reduce factuality and faithfulness hallucinations, addressing trade-offs from separate interventions.

papers.title: Poison as Cure: Visual Noise for Mitigating Object Hallucinations in LVMs
papers.tldr: VAP reduces object hallucinations by optimizing beneficial visual noise while leaving the underlying vision-language model unchanged.

papers.title: Robust Hallucination Detection in LLMs via Adaptive Token Selection
papers.tldr: HaMI jointly learns which token representations to inspect and how to detect hallucinations, improving robustness across varied generated responses.

papers.title: SECA: Semantically Equivalent and Coherent Attacks for Eliciting LLM Hallucinations
papers.tldr: SECA finds coherent, meaning-preserving prompt changes that elicit hallucinations, with higher attack success and almost no constraint violations in its evaluations.

papers.title: Seeing is Believing? Mitigating OCR Hallucinations in Multimodal Large Language Models
papers.tldr: A degraded-document benchmark and uncertainty-aware training reduce unsupported OCR answers, with strong reported gains on KIE-HVQA.

papers.title: Systematic Reward Gap Optimization for Mitigating VLM Hallucinations
papers.tldr: TPR rewrites selected response topics to control preference reward gaps and improve hallucination reduction in vision-language models.

papers.title: The Curse of Multi-Modalities: Evaluating Hallucinations of Large Multimodal Models across Language, Visual, and Audio
papers.tldr: The CMM benchmark investigates multimodal hallucinations linked to overreliance on single-modality priors and misleading cross-modality correlations.

papers.title: The Mirage of Performance Gains: Why Contrastive Decoding Fails to Mitigate Object Hallucinations in MLLMs?
papers.tldr: The paper finds that observed contrastive-decoding gains stem from output-selection effects rather than effective mitigation of object hallucinations.

papers.title: VideoHallu: Evaluating and Mitigating Multi-modal Hallucinations on Synthetic Video Understanding
papers.tldr: VideoHallu exposes failures to recognize impossible video events and shows that targeted post-training can improve detection.

papers.title: When Semantics Mislead Vision: Mitigating Large Multimodal Models Hallucinations in Scene Text Spotting and Understanding
papers.tldr: A training-free framework locates scene text and guides decoding with better-grounded internal layers to reduce semantically plausible but visually incorrect answers.

papers.title: Why and How LLMs Hallucinate: Connecting the Dots with Subsequence Associations
papers.tldr: The paper explains hallucinations through competing learned subsequence associations and introduces a tracing method to identify their causes.

papers.title: A Geometric Analysis of Small-sized Language Model Hallucinations
papers.tldr: Repeated answers exhibit geometric patterns that help identify hallucinations in small language models using relatively few annotations.

papers.title: Adaptive Residual-Update Steering for Low-Overhead Hallucination Mitigation in Large Vision-Language Models
papers.tldr: RUDDER adaptively reinforces visual evidence during generation, reducing object hallucinations while retaining more than 96% of throughput in the reported experiments.

papers.tldr: AFS uses disagreements between model layers to create token-level training rewards that reduce visual hallucinations while preserving caption recall.

papers.title: Are VLMs Seeing or Just Saying? Uncovering the Illusion of Visual Re-examination

papers.title: Attention Sinks as Internal Signals for Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models

papers.title: Automatic Layer Selection for Hallucination Detection
papers.tldr: FEPoID automatically selects informative internal layers for hallucination detection, with further gains from a generation truncation strategy.

papers.title: Beyond Attention Imbalance: Mitigating Hallucinations via Spectral Surgery
papers.tldr: FLASH reduces vision-language hallucinations by modifying the spectral structure of visual attention during decoding, without training or contrastive decoding.

papers.title: Beyond Blind Noising: Disentangled Visual Rectification for Hallucination Mitigation in MLLMs
papers.tldr: DVR separates visual corruption from hallucination-related drift to improve training-free hallucination mitigation in multimodal language models.

papers.title: Beyond Logits: Coherent Hallucination Mitigation via Attention Contrastive Decoding
papers.tldr: Attention Contrastive Decoding complements existing decoding methods to reduce hallucinations while improving output coherence.

papers.title: Building Reliable Long-Form Generation via Hallucination Rejection Sampling
papers.tldr: SHARS reduces long-form hallucinations by detecting, rejecting, and regenerating suspect segments before continuing.

papers.title: Correcting Visual Blur Induced by Attention Distraction to Reduce Hallucinations: Algorithm and Theory
papers.tldr: AFIP reduces object hallucinations without additional training by addressing inconsistent visual attention and its fading during generation.

papers.title: Debate with Images: Detecting Deceptive Behaviors in Multimodal Large Language Models
papers.tldr: A multimodal deception benchmark and visually grounded debate framework improve agreement with human judgments of deceptive model behavior.

papers.title: DEGAP: Dynamic Entropy-Guided Attention Perturbation for Contrastive Decoding in Large Vision-Language Models
papers.tldr: DEGAP dynamically perturbs internal visual attention for contrastive decoding, reducing hallucinations and improving visual question answering across seven benchmarks.

papers.title: Detecting Contextual Hallucinations in Large Language Models with Frequency-Aware Attention
papers.tldr: Rapid local changes in attention provide lightweight features for detecting contextual hallucinations, improving results on two benchmarks.

papers.title: Dismantling Pathological Shortcuts: A Causal Framework for Faithful LVLM Decoding
papers.tldr: Fox identifies and interrupts attention pathways that bypass visual evidence, improving grounded decoding without retraining.

papers.title: DOUBT: Decoupled Object-level Understanding and Bridging via vMF-based Trustworthiness for Hallucination Detection in MLLMs

papers.title: Efficient Hallucination Detection for LLMs Using Uncertainty-Aware Attention Heads
papers.tldr: RAUQ combines internal attention patterns and token confidence to detect potential hallucinations without labels and with less than 1% extra computation.

papers.title: Finding the Correct Visual Evidence Without Forgetting: Mitigating Hallucination in LVLMs via Inter-Layer Visual Attention Discrepancy
papers.tldr: ILVAD uses differences in attention across layers to identify visual evidence and keep generated responses grounded in it without additional training.

papers.tldr: EPGS detects confident factual errors through gradient sensitivity to noisy input embeddings, motivated by a hypothesis that brittle hallucinations occupy sharper minima.

papers.title: From Out-of-Distribution Detection to Hallucination Detection: A Geometric View
papers.tldr: Adapting out-of-distribution detection to next-token prediction yields training-free hallucination detectors with strong reported accuracy on reasoning tasks.

papers.title: Hallucination is a Consequence of Space-Optimality: A Rate-Distortion Theorem for Membership Testing
papers.tldr: A rate-distortion theorem shows how memory-optimal compression of sparse, unstructured facts can produce confident false claims in an idealized setting.

papers.title: HaloProbe: Bayesian Detection and Mitigation of Object Hallucinations in Vision-Language Models
papers.tldr: HaloProbe accounts for confounded attention signals to estimate hallucination probabilities and guide decoding while preserving caption utility and fluency.

papers.title: Harnessing Reasoning Trajectories for Hallucination Detection via Answer-agreement Representation Shaping
papers.tldr: ARS uses answer agreement under small latent perturbations to learn representations that improve hallucination detection without human training labels.

papers.title: How do Humans Process AI-generated Hallucination Contents: a Neuroimaging Study
papers.tldr: EEG recordings reveal distinct neural responses when people correctly recognize versus misjudge hallucinated AI image descriptions.

papers.title: Instruction Lens Score: Your Instruction Contributes a Powerful Object Hallucination Detector for Multimodal Large Language Models
papers.tldr: InsLen detects object hallucinations using instruction-token representations and contextual consistency, without extra training or auxiliary models.

papers.title: IRIS: Implicit Reward-Guided Internal Sifting for Mitigating Multimodal Hallucination
papers.tldr: IRIS reduces multimodal hallucination by ranking self-generated responses with internal rewards and learning from the resulting preference pairs.

papers.tldr: IC-VCO uses shared-context image comparisons and precise visual edits to improve training against multimodal hallucinations.

papers.tldr: MACD uses model feedback to construct targeted visual counterfactuals that reduce video-model hallucinations during decoding.

papers.tldr: A training-free intervention reduces visual hallucinations by selectively suppressing text pathways that overpower image evidence during token decisions.

papers.tldr: MGAP selectively attenuates language-prior components during multimodal decoding, reducing hallucinations while preserving coherent representation structure.

papers.tldr: SCPO uses an easy-to-hard semantic preference curriculum to reduce visual hallucinations while preserving general vision-language performance.

papers.tldr: MM-Snowball measures accumulating visual hallucinations in dialogue, and CAVR mitigates them by refreshing visual grounding and adjusting output scores.

papers.tldr: The authors propose matching expressed uncertainty to a model’s own uncertainty as a way to reduce confident errors while preserving usefulness.

papers.tldr: The paper proposes separating incoherent errors from coherent exploratory hypotheses and evaluating discovery through calibrated novelty plus external validation.

papers.tldr: REVIS reduces object hallucination by selectively restoring suppressed visual information inside vision-language models without retraining.

papers.title: RLSF-V: Mitigating Hallucinations in MLLMs via Fuzzy Semantic Self-Feedback
papers.tldr: RLSF-V uses internal confidence signals to create its own response preferences for reducing multimodal hallucinations without external supervision.

papers.title: Steer Where It Matters: Token-Level Visual-Sensitivity Steering for LVLMs Hallucination Mitigation
